sources.note: Nothing. 4.2 Phonétique et phonologie (pp. 139-148) covers vowels, consonants, 4.2.3 'Tons en tofoké de Yangole' (p. 148: 'Il existe deux tons de base: ton bas et ton haut', tonal minimal pairs) and 4.2.4 syllable structure (V, (N)CV); no mention of accent/stress in the chapter (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent pp. 139-157 and visual read of pp. 139, 148); no accent section anywhere in the book's TOC.

sources.citation: Harries, Lyndon. 1955. Grammar of Gesogo. Kongo-Overzee 21: 420-440.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.15.6.2); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.15.6.2
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Phonetic Data' (pp. 420-421): seven vowels, adjacent vowels realised long, 'Alternance of vowel-length is a grammatical, not a lexical feature'; 'Tonal Data' 4.1-4.4: 'Gesogo is a language with lexical tone', four nominal tone-groups, 'The tone-pattern of words is maintained in all observed syntactical positions', H/L/falling/rising/mid marking. The word 'accent' occurs only as the name of tone diacritics.

sources.citation: Stapleton, Walter H. 1903. Comparative Handbook of Congo Languages. Yakusu: BMS.
sources.note: Has an 'On Accent' section (stem-initial main accent in 'the Congo languages', penult secondary) but the languages compared are Kongo, Bangi, Lolo, Ngala, Poto, Soko, Kele, Swahili — Topoke/Poke is not among them (Foma and Turumbu only mentioned as neighbours); not usable for poke1238.
